A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed from ControlMM to MaskControl. Their complete main texts and appendices, including readable figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original HumanML3D generation and body-editing results, component ablations, timing measurements and embedding analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original HumanML3D experiments and additionally reports human-scene objective-control and STMC timeline evaluations.

M1.justification: The core control branch and logit/embedding optimization framework remain. v2 revises the stated training to retrain MoMask with all-token cross-entropy (Section 3.2, Appendix A.4), and adds an STMC-specific pipeline using SINC filling, transition padding and final text-free synthesis (A.2). DES largely matches v1's weighted-sampling DCSE estimator in A.10.

E1.justification: HumanML3D joint control and upper-body editing remain. v2 adds head-height and square-confinement evaluations, formal barrier-avoidance testing, and STMC timelines with longer sequences and different controllable joint groupings. These substantially extend evaluated conditions beyond v1's joint-control experiments and illustrative obstacle/timeline applications.

E2.justification: MotionLCM joins the pelvis-control and upper-body-editing comparisons and the qualitative trajectory comparison. New objective-control experiments compare against ProgMoGen, unconstrained MDM and MoMask; the timeline evaluation adds STMC-MotionDiffuse and STMC-MDM. Several were cited in v1 but were not evaluated in these comparisons.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce constraint error, unsuccessful rate and maximum joint acceleration, plus STMC per-crop retrieval, TMR scores and transition distance. The density study also changes its stated setting from v1's fixed 196-frame formulation to percentages of 40–196-frame sequences. Retained scores do not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 substantially reduces component diagnostics: v1 Table 3's logit-only and logit-plus-control-branch tests without embedding editing disappear, as do the qualitative component comparison and mask-embedding t-SNE analysis. Other configurations survive in the speed and iteration tables, alongside retained density and confidence analyses. New STMC padding variants test transition handling.

E5.justification: Neither version reports evaluation seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations or significance tests. The retained token-confidence plots describe model predictions rather than uncertainty in experimental performance.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results: Table 4 reports head-height constraint error 0.000 versus ProgMoGen's 0.012 and FID 0.246 versus 0.556; Table 6 reports STMC-comparison FIDs of 0.511 and 0.508. MotionLCM results and a TLControl average row are added, while some ablation results disappear. Legacy pelvis FID 0.061 and upper-body FID 0.074 remain; error-unit conversions are not performance changes.

T1.justification: v2 explicitly defines the spatially conditioned all-token logits loss and changes the printed Gumbel-Softmax denominator. Its DES expectation largely restates v1 Appendix A.10's weighted-embedding construction. The motion-consistency objective and gradient-update reasoning remain, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: v2 narrows the headline performance claim by dropping simultaneous real-time generation and the 20-times-speed claim from the abstract and contribution narrative, although speed claims remain in the appendix. It foregrounds DES as a contribution. High-fidelity, precise masked control and arbitrary-objective optimization were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: v2 Appendix A.2 newly qualifies direct STMC applicability because of different joints and longer sequences, explaining its optimization-based workaround and potential retraining benefit. It also claims superiority across all STMC metrics, although transition distance only ties or trails STMC-MotionDiffuse. The earlier qualification about out-of-distribution body-part prompting remains.

D1.justification: v2 adds inference pseudocode, specifies modified MoMask pretraining and position-only control, and explicitly describes concatenating relative-motion feedback. Most architecture, optimizer, guidance and hardware details remain. Conversely, v1's mask-embedding reconstruction explanation and detailed preprocessing, random-keyframe sampling and density-averaging instructions are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds Cohan et al.'s CondMDI work and removes Hosseyni et al.'s BAD citation. The introduction and new Table 1 more explicitly distinguish TLControl's feed-forward optimization, latent diffusion and masked control. The broader literature coverage and first-controllable-masked-model positioning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten, with pervasive component renaming. The former appendix sampling explanation becomes a dedicated main-text section, evaluation prose is compressed, and the appendices are reorganized around new comparison and algorithm sections.

P2.justification: v2 changes the main text to two columns and replaces separate architecture diagrams with a combined training, sampling and inference figure. It revises the teaser and qualitative comparisons, moves the detailed joint table and speed plot into the appendix, restructures ablation tables, and adds objective-control and STMC displays while removing diagnostic figures.

improvement.justification: Tables 4 and 6 provide quantitative evidence for zero-shot and timeline applicability that v1 largely illustrated, while MotionLCM comparisons and inference pseudocode improve assessment of the method. These gains are partly offset by lost component diagnostics and reproducibility details, plus the overstated all-metric STMC conclusion. The added evidence supports a modest net improvement rather than a substantial overall quality gain.
